points.text: Simple/Hard classification relative to batch pass ratio is noisy; skewed batches yield suboptimal rewards.
Correctness-conditioned length reward never triggers on hardest problems with zero correct responses.
Near-zero length variance makes standardized length unstable; sensitive to decoding hyperparameters and model state.
Tension between exploration-favoring pass@32 training signal and pass@1 evaluation.
Main comparison only against DeepMath-Zero; missing other adaptive length-reward methods.
Fixed length penalty/bonus ablation baselines are strawmen.
Pass@32-length trend may be a statistical artifact of more exploration, not difficulty.
No correlation reported between ground-truth difficulty labels and response length.
Batch-dependent difficulty classification is inconsistent and may give unstable training signals.
Missing comparison with popular length penalties (Kimi-1.5) or overlong filtering.
Should validate on Qwen-3 series models.
No ablation over hyperparameters beta and alpha.
Length Bonus has longer responses but lower performance, contradicting claim longer helps hard problems.
Typos (infeasbile, effciency).
No ablation isolating dual reward vs model-aware difficulty contributions.
Length bonus/penalty variants too simplistic to explain accuracy gains.
No sensitivity study on alpha, beta, lambda.
Pass@1 decreases with length, contradicting motivation that longer reasoning helps hard problems.
Difficulty classification via group pass ratio is circular; may cause instability or bias.
Unclear how dual reward integrates into policy gradient; no formal analysis of effects on updates.
Lacks baselines against RL reasoning-compression works and positioning among them.
Batch-reliant difficulty measure unstable; fluctuates with batch composition.
Unclear how hyperparameters (beta = ±1) were determined.
Effect of group size G not studied.
Missing control DAPO run without length reward; gains not attributable to dual reward.
No efficiency baselines (Kimi 1.5, L1, SFT compression) are run.
SOTA and outperforms-all claims rest on one baseline and are not literally true (tie).
No accuracy-vs-length trade-off curves against other methods.
Single run per model; no seeds or confidence intervals for small gains.
Checkpoint selected on validation set including AIME; baselines may not get same selection.
Length Bonus ablation results conflict between Fig. 4c and Table 2, unexplained.
Ablations on 7B only.
No ablation of Hard/Simple assignment, conditional reward, or EMA vs raw batch ratio.
No sensitivity analysis for alpha and lambda.
Binned pass@32 preliminary analysis conflates truncation and subset effects; does not show wider coverage.
Preliminary trend fails on 7B AIME25, rescued post hoc with k=64; no bin sizes or CIs.
Claim that length penalties restrict reasoning boundary untested; no large-k pass@k for final models.
Hard is relative to batch mean, so about half of every batch is always Hard.
EMA initialization of batch pass ratio creates an early length-bonus artifact.
Small beta and alpha magnitudes unlikely to drive 58% compression; no reward distribution shown.
Length reward applies only to correct responses, which are scarce for hard problems.
Difficulty-adaptive length allocation never measured; no length vs difficulty plot.
Entropy-leads-to-performance claim is correlational.
Reflection analysis uses unvalidated GPT-4o judge, tiny differences, selective behavior reporting.
Math domain only; no code or science tasks.
Only Qwen2.5 3B/7B; no larger, other-family or distilled reasoning models.
Behavior beyond 10K training cap not analyzed.
Efficiency measured only as mean response length.
Many typos and inconsistent Simple/Easy wording.
Overloaded notation for beta, R_z, R_l.
Overstated language (perfectly, intelligently).
Missing details: baseline training budget, bin formation, exact length tables.

P.summary: Batch-relative difficulty classification noisy, circular and unstable
No length signal for problems with zero correct responses
Standardized length unstable with low variance
Pass@1 falls with length, conflicting with motivation/training signal
Preliminary pass@32 trend may be artifact
No validation of length vs true difficulty

Q.summary: No trade-off curves vs other methods
Preliminary trend fails, rescued post hoc
Reward magnitude too small to explain compression
Length reward only on scarce correct responses
